channel.title: AI Frontier Post
channel.description: Dispatches from the AI frontier: AI news, research explainers, frontier lab coverage, and product comparisons.

item.title: Colibri v2.1.0: run GGUF models as-is and use the new chat UI — hands-on
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Colibri (JustVugg/colibri, Apache-2.0, 47,760 GitHub stars at the 4 November 2026 check) runs huge open mixture-of-experts models on the machine you already have. Version 2.1.0, released 31 October 2026, reads published GGUF files exactly as they are — no conversion — and adds a new chat UI. This guide installs v2.1.0, imports a GGUF, opens the new UI, and points your other apps at the local server.

item.title: GitHub Copilot comes to Xcode's built-in coding assistant in public preview
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: GitHub said on November 4, 2026, that Copilot now works directly in Xcode's built-in coding assistant, in public preview starting with Xcode 27.3 beta. It needs macOS Tahoe 26.6 or later, supports all Copilot plans, and leaves the existing Copilot for Xcode extension as a separate option.

item.title: OpenAI to acquire Pierre Computer, bringing Code Storage and Codex's Trees and Diffs libraries in-house
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: OpenAI said on November 4, 2026, that it will acquire Pierre Computer Company, Inc., maker of Code Storage and the Trees and Diffs libraries already used in the Codex app. Code Storage features will move into Codex, Pierre's open-source projects will stay open source, and no price was disclosed.

item.title: Leidos HeadWay Dispatch: AI agent governance that lets operators block, approve, or auto-run agent actions
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Leidos introduced HeadWay Dispatch on November 4, 2026, a platform for governing AI agents from different vendors with three controls — Know, Control, and Prove — plus calibrated autonomy, a tamper-evident Flight Recorder, and a kill switch that works without cloud connectivity.

item.title: TestGrid ONE launches: an AI operating system for quality engineering that runs Selenium, Playwright and Appium suites as written
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: TestGrid launched TestGrid ONE on November 4, 2026: the successor to TestOS that pairs AI agents — CoTester for test generation and AgentRx for self-healing — with real-device and browser infrastructure, running existing Selenium, Playwright and Appium suites without conversion.

item.title: SWE-2 Flash: Cognition's new coding model for Devin runs 3x faster at one-fifth the price of SWE-2
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Cognition launched SWE-2 Flash on November 4, 2026, for Devin Desktop and CLI: a coding model built from Thinking Machines' Inkling-Small that runs three times faster than SWE-2 at one-fifth the price — free through November 30, with its weights held back over cybersecurity risks.

item.title: NeuralGCM+: Google gives Ai2 $5M to turn its AI weather model into a climate projector for decades ahead
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Google.org is giving the Allen Institute for AI about $5 million, plus $1.8 million in cloud credits, to build NeuralGCM+, an open-source model that extends Google Research's NeuralGCM from weather forecasts of up to a year to climate projections spanning 5 to 50 years.

item.title: RustXNG: give your AI agent its own private web search — hands-on with v0.27.1
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: RustXNG (sahenjp/RustXNG, AGPL-3.0, 815 GitHub stars at the 4 November 2026 check) is a self-hosted metasearch engine in Rust, based on SearXNG: one loopback binary that fans a query out to upstream engines and returns ranked JSON an agent can use, plus a read-only MCP server with search and read_page tools. This guide installs the v0.27.1 release binary, verifies it, and wires it into an agent — with the provider-terms caveat the project itself puts first.

item.title: Nothing's first AI-native device ships in December: a screenless work tool with no new display
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Nothing CEO Carl Pei confirmed on November 4 that the company's first AI-native product ships in December: a screenless work tool built as dedicated hardware, not an app. No name, price, or specifications yet.

item.title: Fresche X-Modernize AI goes self-service: IBM i teams can convert RPG to Java themselves, starting with 1,000 free credits
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Fresche Solutions has released X-Modernize AI as a self-service web app, letting IBM i development teams analyze their applications and convert RPG code to Java on their own. New accounts start with 1,000 credits and no credit card; the same engine previously ran only through Fresche's managed Modernization-as-a-Service.

item.title: Kimi K3.1 Pro open weights are live: Moonshot's 2.8T model lands on Hugging Face on its promised date
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Moonshot AI's Kimi K3.1 Pro weights are now public on Hugging Face as moonshotai/Kimi-K3.1-Pro, on the November 4 date Moonshot promised at the model's October 23 launch. The 2.8-trillion-parameter model keeps its 1M-token context and ships under its own Kimi K3.1 Pro License.

item.title: Shackleton AI emerges from stealth: AI agents for construction paperwork, backed by a $5M Battery Ventures seed round
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Shackleton AI emerged from stealth on November 4, 2026, unveiling an agentic platform that unifies construction work from site selection to turnover and puts AI agents on administrative tasks. It raised $5 million in seed funding led by Battery Ventures.

item.title: Nooks launches its Revenue Agent Platform and lands a $500M General Catalyst commitment to automate sales end to end
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Nooks formally launched its Revenue Agent Platform on November 4, 2026, alongside a $500 million commitment from General Catalyst's Customer Value Fund to finance its sales and marketing push. The platform covers sales work from first contact to renewal; the funding is a share of returns, not an equity stake.

item.title: Together Compiler: AI agents that rewrite GPU code to make open models faster overnight
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Together AI launched Together Compiler on November 4, 2026: teams of AI agents that rewrite the GPU code behind open-source models, reaching state-of-the-art optimizations within 24 hours, according to the company. It is already running on many of Together's most popular serverless endpoints.

item.title: CleanYourTV: debloat your Android TV and get an Apple TV-style home screen — hands-on
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: CleanYourTV (Gathin23/cleanyourtv, MIT, 51,716 GitHub stars at the 4 November 2026 check) debloats any Android TV or Google TV over Wi-Fi with a coding assistant: it backs up, disables bloat with pm disable-user, and installs a 572 KB launcher — with nothing uninstalled and a one-line restore. This guide follows the project's README and prompt, step by step.

item.title: Sectra Reporting at Mount Sinai: AI-assisted radiology reporting for 1.2 million exams a year
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Sectra signed a seven-year agreement with Mount Sinai Health System on November 4, 2026, to deliver Sectra Reporting, its AI-assisted radiology reporting module, across all of the New York health system's radiology services — more than 1.2 million exams a year. Go-live is planned for spring 2027.

item.title: UN Toolbox for People-Centred Smart Cities in the AI Era: human control first for city AI
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: The United Nations launched the U4SSC Toolbox for People-Centred Smart Cities in the AI Era on November 4, 2026, in Barcelona. Issued by the ITU and UN-Habitat, it gives mayors and city managers guidance for keeping public decisions under meaningful human control as AI moves into city services.

item.title: Cerillion 26.2 adds agentic AI to telecom billing: customer care, package design and churn prediction
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Cerillion announced the general availability of Cerillion 26.2 on November 4, 2026, expanding agentic AI across its telecom BSS/OSS suite with a Customer Care Agent, a Service Configuration Agent, competitor-aware package design and Predictive Churn, under centralised model governance and open APIs.

item.title: Tencent Hy4 launches: 770B model adds vision and Computer Use, with open weights to follow
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Tencent Hunyuan released the official version of Hy4 on November 4, 2026: a 770-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model that adds visual understanding and Computer Use for the first time. The weights are to be open-sourced soon; Hy4 is already live via Tencent Cloud and OpenRouter.

item.title: Audit your Android phone for leaks: hands-on with NOIR over adb
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: NOIR (Verlintas/NOIR, MIT, 1,831 GitHub stars at the 4 November 2026 check) audits your own Android phone over adb — permissions, APK endpoints and data flows — with no root, no account and no uploads. This guide installs v0.2.5, scans read-only, reads the report and its three domain lists, and applies only reversible fixes.

item.title: Netflix launches AI Discover: a TV tab that recommends by mood, starting with a small group of US viewers
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Netflix announced AI Discover on November 3, 2026: a new experimental tab in its TV app whose first feature recommends shows and films from themed collections such as “Scare me” and “Family movie night”, powered by a new intelligence layer. It is starting to roll out in the US, in English, on supported TVs.

item.title: Nordic's nRF71 puts Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and edge AI on one chip built to run for years on a battery
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Nordic Semiconductor announced the nRF71 Series on November 3, 2026: Wi-Fi, Bluetooth LE, Thread and edge AI on a single chip, with up to 20 times lower standby power than its nRF70 Wi-Fi products. The first two parts are sampling with selected customers.

item.title: Study any website, then rebuild it clean-room: hands-on with Craft Anything
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Craft Anything (storytold/craft-anything, MIT OR Apache-2.0, 8,386 GitHub stars in its first three days) studies a website, app or game with 320 inspection tools and has a coding agent rebuild it from evidence, checking the result at three screen widths. This guide installs it, inspects example.com without any AI, runs a clean-room rebuild, and states plainly what is still early alpha.

item.title: Google launches Guided Learning in Classroom worldwide, pilots it in Search — and turns school AI off by default
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Google announced on November 3, 2026 that Guided Learning is now globally available in Google Classroom, with a Search pilot starting in select U.S. schools later this month — and that Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom and Google Search will be off for K-12 student accounts until administrators turn them on.

item.title: Straive and Anthropic partner to deploy enterprise AI responsibly, with governance and human oversight
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Straive announced a partnership with Anthropic on November 3, 2026, pairing Anthropic’s AI models with Straive’s governance, domain expertise and human oversight to help enterprises build, deploy and run AI in industry-specific workflows.
